title: These easily reconcile freedom with the decrees: the decrees follow the foreseen determination, so only consequent necessity arises
source_text: XXIII. Facile autem isti conciliant arbitrii nostri libertatem cum decretis divinis; quandoquidem juxta ipsos, decreta Divina sequuntur praevisionem determinationis, quae a voluntate nostra futura est, tanquam prima ejus radice & causa. Ac proinde non magis ex decretis Divinis quam ex Dei praescientia, ulla oritur in nostris actionibus necessitas praecedens, sed solum sequens, quae non tollit, sed integram supponit nostram libertatem.
pass_a_gloss: XXIII. But these easily reconcile the freedom of our choice with the divine decrees; since according to them, the Divine decrees follow the prevision of the determination which is to be from our will, as its first root and cause. And therefore no more from the Divine decrees than from God's foreknowledge does any preceding necessity arise in our actions, but only a following one, which does not take away, but supposes entire our freedom.
pass_b_english: These men find it easy to reconcile the freedom of our choice with God's decrees. On their view the divine decrees follow God's foresight of the determination that will come from our will as its first root and cause.

So the divine decrees, no more than God's foreknowledge, give rise to any preceding necessity in our actions. They produce only a consequent necessity, which does not remove our freedom but presupposes it intact.

lemmas.gloss: as its first root and cause
preceding necessity, but only a following one

choices.why: Necessity that precedes and so constrains the act, contrasted with consequent or concomitant necessity; kept as technical terms.
